dates.notes: The GGE adopted its final report by consensus on 4 September 2026. The Seventh Review Conference adopted its final document on 20 November 2026 (to be issued as CCW/CONF.VII/11), endorsing the set of elements and continuing the GGE. The 2027 sessions are scheduled for 1–5 March and 30 August–3 September 2027.

ai_provisions: Working characterisation of lethal autonomous weapons systems
Application of international law in armed conflict, including international humanitarian law and the principles of distinction, proportionality and precautions in attack
Human control and judgement required for compliance with applicable international humanitarian law
Human responsibility and accountability that cannot be transferred to machines
Specific prohibitions, restrictions and risk-mitigation measures, including measures relating to the human element
Other possible measures and a recommendation on the legal nature and specific form of the instrument, including whether it should be a binding protocol
relevance.excluded_scope: The 2026 report is not a draft protocol and creates no legal obligations. The Review Conference mandate is to elaborate an instrument by consensus, without prejudging its nature; no instrument has been adopted. The record covers the negotiation, not an adopted treaty.
relevance.reason: The CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS is the principal multilateral negotiating track on lethal autonomous weapons systems. Its 2024–2026 final report sets out a working characterisation of LAWS, the applicable legal framework, human control and judgement, possible prohibitions and restrictions, accountability, and other possible measures. The Seventh Review Conference endorsed the set of elements on 20 November 2026 and continued the Group with a mandate to elaborate an instrument, without prejudging its nature, and to recommend its legal form, including a binding protocol.

status_note: No instrument has been adopted. The 2024–2026 GGE adopted its final report by consensus on 4 September 2026. The Seventh Review Conference (16–20 November 2026) endorsed the set of elements of an instrument and other possible measures and continued the open-ended GGE, mandating it to elaborate, by consensus, an instrument that specifies international humanitarian law applicable to LAWS and its implementation, without prejudging the instrument's nature, and to recommend its legal nature and specific form, including whether it should be a binding protocol. The Group is to report to the 2028 Meeting of High Contracting Parties.
